1.explanation: Both of these demo-markdown files include a CSS snippet near the bottom that reads “.next-select { margin-right: 8px; margin-bottom: 8px; }”. Because it’s defined at the top level of the demo CSS block, every Select in the documentation gets that extra bottom margin, breaking the layout of other demo examples. Removing or scoping out the ‘margin-bottom: 8px’ rule in these files will prevent the unwanted spacing.
1.bug_scenario: In the Select component documentation demos, a global CSS block in the markdown files unconditionally applies “.next-select { margin-bottom: 8px; }” to every Select instance. This fixed margin spills over into all examples (single, multiple, combobox, etc.), causing unwanted spacing and viewport scroll issues across demos.

2.explanation: Both combobox-basic.md and select-basic.md include a CSS code block that declares “.next-select { margin-right: 8px; margin-bottom: 8px; }” at the root level. That global selector causes every Select on the page to get an 8px bottom margin, even in demos that shouldn’t. Removing or scoping that style to the demo’s container will prevent it from affecting other examples.
2.bug_scenario: In the Select component’s documentation demo pages, two of the markdown demo files add a global CSS rule targeting “.next-select { margin-bottom: 8px; }”. Because this rule is not scoped to a specific demo container it applies to every Select trigger on the page, leading to inconsistent spacing and broken layouts in demos that don’t expect that bottom margin.
